about.title: Organization profile
about.subtitle: About Tatsumi Cooperative
about.greetingBody: Tatsumi Cooperative is a business cooperative established under the Small and Medium-sized Enterprise Cooperatives Act. Founded on mutual support among our member businesses, our purpose is to support their operations through joint purchasing and related activities. We move forward steadily, together with the businesses of our region.

purpose.title: Purpose
purpose.body: Grounded in mutual support among members, we work to stabilise and strengthen their business foundations.

policy.title: Policy
policy.body: We undertake activities that are genuinely worth doing jointly, placing our members' interests first.

stance.title: Stance
stance.body: We comply with applicable legislation and strive for sound, transparent governance.

info.name: Name
info.businessVal:
(1) Joint purchasing of goods required by members
(2) Joint acceptance of foreign technical intern trainees for members, and employment placement relating to such acceptance
(3) Joint acceptance of Ikusei-Shuro foreign nationals for members, and employment placement relating to such acceptance
(4) Support for Specified Skilled Worker foreign nationals on behalf of members
(5) Education and information services to improve members’ management and technology, or to disseminate knowledge relating to the cooperative’s activities
(6) Member welfare programmes
(7) Activities incidental to the above

* Activities (2) to (4) are to begin only after authorization is granted by the relevant authorities. We do not carry them out at present.

tit.title: Technical Intern Training
tit.subtitle: A general overview of the program
tit.overviewTitle: What is the Technical Intern Training program?
tit.overviewBody: The Technical Intern Training program was established to transfer Japanese skills, techniques and knowledge to people from developing countries, contributing to the economic development of their home countries. Across categories 1, 2 and 3, the program allows a maximum stay of five years.
tit.industriesNote: * Eligible occupations and tasks are prescribed by law and reviewed periodically. Please refer to publications by the relevant authorities for the latest details.
tit.flowNote: * This illustrates the general flow prescribed by the program.
tit.faqTitle: Frequently asked questions about the program

faq.q1: How long is the period of stay?
faq.a1: Across categories 1, 2 and 3, the program allows a maximum of five years. Requirements are prescribed for each category.
faq.a2: Eligible occupations and tasks are prescribed by law and reviewed periodically. Please refer to publications by the relevant authorities for the latest details.
faq.a3: This varies by occupation and category. In some fields, such as nursing care, language requirements apply at entry.
faq.q4: What happens with the transition to Ikusei-Shuro?
faq.a4: The Ikusei-Shuro program takes effect on April 1, 2027. Transitional measures apply to people who are in technical intern training on that date, among others. Please refer to publications by the relevant authorities for details.

tit.sourceNote: Source: compiled as general information from materials published by the Immigration Services Agency, the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, and OTIT.
tit.disclaimer: This page provides a general explanation of the program. It does not indicate that this cooperative conducts a supervising and support business; that business is currently under application for authorization.

ssw.title: Ikusei-Shuro
ssw.subtitle: A general overview of the program
ssw.overviewBody: The Ikusei-Shuro program was created to develop and secure foreign human resources, and takes effect on April 1, 2027. Through three years of employment in principle, it develops workers to the skill level of Specified Skilled Worker (i), while securing human resources in fields facing labour shortages in Japan.
ssw.diffTitle: Main differences from Technical Intern Training

rows: 3 years in principle (transition to SSW envisaged)
Permitted where circumstances leave no alternative, and also at the person’s own initiative if certain requirements are met
Levels and tests are set for each industrial field and job category

period.title: Three years of development in principle
period.desc: Through three years of employment in principle, workers improve their skills and Japanese-language ability and are developed to the level of Specified Skilled Worker (i).

continuity.title: Continuity with the Specified Skilled Worker system
continuity.desc: The program is designed with continuity to the Specified Skilled Worker system. By acquiring the required skills and Japanese-language ability through Ikusei-Shuro and meeting the necessary requirements, a person can move on to Specified Skilled Worker (i).

transfer.title: Changing employer at the person’s own initiative
transfer.desc: In addition to transfers where circumstances leave no alternative, a person may change employer at their own initiative if certain requirements are met: remaining within the same job category, having passed the transfer-restriction period set for each field (set between one and two years by the field-specific operational policy), and having attained a certain level of skill and Japanese-language ability. The specific requirements differ according to the operational policy for each industrial field.

japanese.title: Improving Japanese-language ability and skills
japanese.desc: The program values not only the acquisition of skills through work but also improvement in Japanese-language ability. The required levels of skill and language ability, and the relevant tests, are set according to the industrial field and job category.

ssw.scheduleNote: * Based on information published as of September 2026. Please refer to publications by the relevant authorities for the latest details.
ssw.sourceNote: Source: compiled as general information from materials published by the Immigration Services Agency (including its Ikusei-Shuro Q&A) and the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (as of September 2026).
ssw.disclaimer: This page provides a general explanation of the program. It does not indicate that this cooperative conducts a supervising and support business; that business is currently under application for authorization.
ssw.orgBody:
Towards the start of the Ikusei-Shuro program, Tatsumi Cooperative is applying for a Supervising & Support Organization license and building its support structure for accepting workers.
The supervising and support business is currently under application for authorization, and we do not carry out the duties of a Supervising & Support Organization.
Once authorization is granted by the relevant authorities, we plan to begin a properly conducted supervising and support business in accordance with the law and the applicable operational guidelines.
ssw.supportBody:
So that foreign workers can work and live in Japan with peace of mind, we are building our support structure in cooperation with the companies that accept them.
At present we are putting in place support in Khmer (Cambodian).
We will expand that structure in line with future circumstances.

ssk.title: Specified Skilled Worker
ssk.subtitle: A general overview of the residence status
ssk.overviewBody: Specified Skilled Worker is a residence status created in 2019 to accept foreign nationals with a certain level of expertise and skill in fields facing serious labour shortages. Skill level and Japanese-language ability are confirmed through examinations prescribed for each field.

n1.title: Category 1
n1.desc: For work requiring skills that call for a substantial degree of knowledge or experience. The period of stay is capped at five years in total.

n2.title: Category 2
n2.desc: For work requiring proficient skills. There is no overall cap on renewals of the period of stay.

ssk.fieldsBody: Covered fields include nursing care, construction, agriculture and manufacturing, among others. Fields are added and revised as the system is amended.
ssk.fieldsNote: * Covered fields and their requirements are reviewed periodically. Please refer to publications by the relevant authorities for the latest details.
ssk.diffTitle: Differences from Technical Intern Training and Ikusei-Shuro

rows: Cat. 1: 5 years total / Cat. 2: no cap
